scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Apanomeritis originated in Crete, Greece, where it was primarily performed in central regions such as Rethymno and Heraklion until shortly after the war.
Though historically a mixed dance performed by both men and women, in modern practice it is danced mainly by women.
on_screen: Map: Greece · Europe
Image — MISSING

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: The dance is alternatively known as provatinistikos, meaning sheep dance, because the stamping footwork reflects the way sheep stamp when agitated or nervous.
It was performed communally until shortly after the war and continues primarily through women's performances.
Today it is a living tradition.
on_screen: Footage: Onze Slag (Adhunik Hanpuriyan Album) (https://archive.org/details/onze-slag-adhunik-hanpuriyan-album)

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: The dance is performed in a circle.
Dancers hold hands palm-to-palm with their hands crossed down.
The footwork consists of a ten-step pattern characterized by dancers stamping their feet against the ground, an action reminiscent of the movements of nervous sheep.
Watch for the Provatinistikos stamp.
